title: A repeatable UX review and redesign workshop
outcome: Review a workflow using task evidence, interaction principles, accessibility, and measurable outcomes.
useCase: Daily frontend reviews and a portfolio-quality workflow redesign.
benefits: Turns UX knowledge into a repeatable engineering/design habit.
drawbacks: A review still needs user and implementation evidence.
version: Web UX · WCAG 2.2 · principles, not magic formulas
cue: A principle is a question to test, not a verdict.

trace.title: Task walkthrough
trace.detail: Use your reading of The Design of Everyday Things and Don’t Make Me Think as a starting point, then apply a repeatable review. Look for a mismatch between what users intend, what the interface suggests, what the system does, and what feedback explains.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
First walk the task yourself. Then inspect controls, grouping, language, feedback, recovery, and access. Then observe another person attempting it. Turn the most consequential finding into a prototype and a focused test.

Keep a small review checklist in daily work: task, context, next action, current state, error prevention, recovery, access, and evidence. Use heuristics to ask questions, not as decorative law names in a design review.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A beautiful mockup can hide missing system states. A law name does not prove a design. A new interaction can increase learning cost even if it looks cleaner.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Review a workflow using task evidence, interaction principles, accessibility, and measurable outcomes. Explain one example and one failure.
